prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Stumptown Coffee Roasters (company_id stumptown-coffee; category: specialty coffee roaster)
Official domains: stumptowncoffee.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Full transparency — we work with producers we know, so both sides of the supply chain stay visible to each other. * Long-term partnership — we sustain these relationships over many years to build truly collaborative partnerships."

[P2] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/sustainability-and-impact | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 1999, 2003 | published: unknown
"1999 STUMPTOWN OPENS ITS DOORS Stumptown launches Holler Mountain, our signature organic coffee blend ### 2003 FIRST DIRECT TRADE RELATIONSHIP First Direct trade sourcing relationship with the Aguirre Family's El Injerto farm in Huehuetenango, Guatemala"

[P3] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 1999 | published: unknown
"Coffee is about pleasure. It’s that moment when your hand is warmed by the mug, you raise it to your nose, inhale deeply, and then take a sip. That sip is the culmination of years of work, three-thousand-mile journeys, and passion. These are the steps we take to ensure that each sip is perfect. Stumptown Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster and retailer founded in Portland, Oregon, in 1999. The first cafe opened on Southeast Division Street in a former beauty parlor called \"Hair Bender,\" which became the name of Stumptown's signature espresso blend. Stumptown now operates cafes in select cities across the US and as far away as Kyoto, Japan."

[P4] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/our-story | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 1999 | published: unknown
"When Stumptown Coffee Roasters opened its first cafe in Portland, Oregon, in 1999, we did so with the belief that the people who grow coffee deserve the same attention as the people who drink it. \"Our primary job in sourcing is to let the coffees do the talking - as a direct reflection of the craft and innovation of the many dedicated producers we have partnered with over the past 20+ years."

[P5] source: https://www.goodandgold.com/work/stumptown-coffee | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Stumptown Coffee A behind-the-scenes look at Stumptown's \"Cold Brew Is Back\" Campaign. ## Goal This campaign's primary objective was to drive online sales of Stumptown Coffee's relaunched cold brew blend, focusing on educating and engaging customers about its unique characteristics. A secondary aim was to boost awareness of Stumptown's range of ready-to-drink cold brew products, highlighting their distinct flavors and retail availability. Additionally, the campaign encouraged visits to Stumptown cafes, showcasing their unique brand experience and deepening customer engagement."

[P6] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/sustainability-and-impact | document: official_domain | type: brand_positioning | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"As our business continues to grow and evolve, so will our Direct Trade model to continue our mission of making the most positive impact where we can. What is organic coffee? According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, \"USDA certified organic foods are grown and processed according to federal guidelines addressing, among many factors, soil quality, animal raising practices, pest and weed control, and use of additives. Organic producers rely on natural substances and physical, mechanical, or biologically based farming methods to the fullest extent possible.\" Coffees can only be designated organic if they've been produced and processed in a manner consistent with these guidelines."

[P7] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/blogs/news | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Huye Mountain: A Rwanda Single Origin Coffee Story Discover Huye Mountain single origin coffee from Rwanda and the story of producer David Rubanzangabo. Explore how quality, community, and innovation shaped one of Stumptown’s longest-standing partnerships."

[P8] source: https://adlibrary.com/brands/stumptown-coffee | document: third_party_confirmed | type: provider_reported_result | flags: vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics | dates in text: 2015 | published: unknown
"Browse Stumptown Coffee's ads on AdLibrary at adlibrary.com. What platforms does Stumptown Coffee advertise on? Instagram, Facebook, and in-store trade marketing through grocery retail channels. Who are Stumptown Coffee's main competitors? Blue Bottle Coffee, Chameleon Cold Brew, and La Colombe in the premium RTD coffee segment. What makes Stumptown Coffee's ads effective? Heritage and specificity — the Hair Bender blend, Portland origin, and direct trade sourcing give copy concrete details that generic coffee brands cannot match. Who owns Stumptown Coffee? Peet's Coffee, itself owned by JAB Holding Company, acquired Stumptown Coffee Roasters in 2015."

[P9] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/pages/sustainability-and-impact | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Partnering With Producers We’re dedicated to sourcing the world’s best coffees while challenging supply chain norms. We do this by honoring our Direct Trade relationships, paying quality premiums for our coffees, and creating multi-year commitments to our producers."

[P10] source: https://www.stumptowncoffee.com/blogs/news | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: 2006 | published: unknown
"Hospitality Stories: Mix Bakeshop Since 2006, Mix Bakeshop has become a sought-out destination for the Ashland, OR community to indulge and nourish themselves with artisan pastries and Direct Trade coffee."

generator.quote_repair: claims.repair_quotes (min similarity 0.9; numbers/negations unchanged); see attempts[].quote_repairs
